Pooled result

MD -5.691 (-7.3 to -4.083), 95% interval

mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure. random-effects, estimator REML (restricted maximum likelihood), k = 2.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 0.2375 on 1 df

Two trials randomise the same fixed-dose combination against the same comparator and register the same continuous endpoint. Nothing had to be harmonised: this review's question was already a question, its estimand was already shared, and its arms already matched. What it lacked was any evidence that these were the only two, and the executed search of 2026-08-19 supplies it -- 57 registrations screened, 53 excluded, and only four carrying both arms of the contrast at all. The other two are long-term open-label safety studies that register no blood-pressure change outcome at any rank, so they are eligible and not poolable rather than absent.

Nothing moved, and that is the result.

Table 6. Nothing moved, and that is the result.
knestimateI²
before the check22156-5.691 (-7.3 to -4.083)0%
after22156-5.691 (-7.3 to -4.083)0%

No trial joined and none left. The pooled estimate is unchanged to every digit.

Before the search, this review's two trials were the two somebody put on a page. They are now the two that the whole 57-record azilsartan programme supports, and the difference between those two states is invisible from the outside -- a correct included set and an unexamined one look identical. The check is what distinguishes them, and it is worth the same when it confirms.

Second instance in one day, by a different route. bococizumab's evidence base was checked and gained a trial; this one was checked and gained none; apixaban's withholding question moved one poolable set UP and another down. A procedure whose answers were always convenient would be indistinguishable from no procedure.

Read this beside the estimate. This pooled outcome is identified as week 8. NCT00846365 registers its primary at week 8; NCT01033071 registers its primary at week 12 -- 'Change From Baseline in Trough, Sitting, Clinic Systolic Blood Pressure', time frame 'Baseline and Week 12'. The measurement is the same measurement in the same words; it is not taken at the same time. GRADE indirectness is rated down for it.

Both trials randomise two experimental arms -- azilsartan/chlorthalidone 20-40mg and 40-80mg -- against one olmesartan/hydrochlorothiazide comparator. This object stores one effect per trial. Which dose contrast it represents, OR whether the two were combined, is not established from the registrations. Recorded as unestablished rather than assumed, because a multi-arm trial contributing one row against a shared control is where control-group double counting arises.

The unadjusted interval is MD -5.6912 (-7.2996 to -4.0828) mmHg and excludes no effect. This project's floored Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is -16.1181 to 4.7357 and includes it. The honest reading is narrow: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives, so this is weaker evidence against the result than the same crossing would be at larger k. Disclosed because a reader is entitled to both intervals.

Stated plainly. No result-level RoB 2 assessment has been performed for either contributing result. That is recorded as unassessed, never as absent of bias, and GRADE is rated down one level for it. What would close it: RoB 2 per result on the clinic systolic pressure outcome in both registrations.

What this does not establishNot that the trials are free of bias -- no RoB-2 assessment is recorded on this object. Not that the pooled value transfers outside the populations these trials enrolled. Not that the registry's posted analysis is itself correct: it is read, and reading it faithfully is a different claim from endorsing it.
Why that is a finding and not a null resultBefore the search, this review's two trials were the two somebody put on a page. They are now the two that the whole 57-record azilsartan programme supports, and the difference between those two states is invisible from the outside -- a correct included set and an unexamined one look identical. The check is what distinguishes them, and it is worth the same when it confirms.
Why absentk=2 and a pool was computed -- it is on this page -- but not by a model call this object can quote. There is no R session, no printed output and no package version, so P6 refuses on the quotation and not on the synthesis. The arithmetic is reproducible from the script named on the outcome; a quotable metafor call is what is missing and what would hold P6.
A the two trials do not measure at the same timeRead this beside the estimate. This pooled outcome is identified as week 8. NCT00846365 registers its primary at week 8; NCT01033071 registers its primary at week 12 -- 'Change From Baseline in Trough, Sitting, Clinic Systolic Blood Pressure', time frame 'Baseline and Week 12'. The measurement is the same measurement in the same words; it is not taken at the same time. GRADE indirectness is rated down for it.
B each trial has two dose arms and this pool carries one effect eachBoth trials randomise two experimental arms -- azilsartan/chlorthalidone 20-40mg and 40-80mg -- against one olmesartan/hydrochlorothiazide comparator. This object stores one effect per trial. Which dose contrast it represents, OR whether the two were combined, is not established from the registrations. Recorded as unestablished rather than assumed, because a multi-arm trial contributing one row against a shared control is where control-group double counting arises.
C the effect does not survive the small sample adjustmentThe unadjusted interval is MD -5.6912 (-7.2996 to -4.0828) mmHg and excludes no effect. This project's floored Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is -16.1181 to 4.7357 and includes it. The honest reading is narrow: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives, so this is weaker evidence against the result than the same crossing would be at larger k. Disclosed because a reader is entitled to both intervals.
D risk of bias has not been assessed on this topicStated plainly. No result-level RoB 2 assessment has been performed for either contributing result. That is recorded as unassessed, never as absent of bias, and GRADE is rated down one level for it. What would close it: RoB 2 per result on the clinic systolic pressure outcome in both registrations.
Why the query is the drug and not the contrastSearching for the contrast -- azilsartan and chlorthalidone and olmesartan -- would have surfaced only trials that already name all three, which is the set this review already holds. A query built from the included set cannot discover anything the included set does not already contain. The whole drug programme is surfaced and the contrast is applied at screening, where it is auditable.
Why 53 of 57 are excluded and that is not a criticism of the queryThe query is the whole azilsartan programme and the review is one fixed-dose combination against one other. All 53 exclusions FAIL on comparator -- only four registrations in the entire programme carry an olmesartan-plus-hydrochlorothiazide arm, and the other fifty-three randomise azilsartan against valsartan, olmesartan alone, ramipril, candesartan, amlodipine, or placebo. All are perfectly good contrasts and none is this one. The query was deliberately built from the drug and not from the contrast: a query built from the contrast could only have returned trials already naming all three agents, which is the set this review already held, and a search that can only confirm the included set is not a search.
And the included set did not changek stays 2. The third direction again, on a second topic and by a different route: bococizumab's evidence base was checked and gained one trial; this one was checked and gained none. Before either search, neither review could tell a correct included set from an unexamined one.
And they are narrow because the question isA review of one fixed-dose combination against one other has narrow criteria by construction, and narrowness is only a defect when it is derived backwards from the trials already present. Every limb below is auditable against a registry field, and the screen was run over the whole 57-record drug programme rather than over a shortlist.
Why it does not settle it aloneA condition that names a study objective is not a statement about the population. NCT01309828 declares `conditions: Safety` while its title reads '...in Hypertensive Subjects With Moderate Renal Impairment', and it carries both arms of this review's contrast. The field is neither absent nor negative; it is uninformative, and excluding on it asserts something the record nowhere says. Where every declared condition names an objective the coded field is not assessable for this limb and the verdict falls back to the title -- and says on its face which it rests on. The fallback still excludes: NCT03652792 declares a bioequivalence objective and its title says 'in Chinese Healthy Volunteers'.
And the included set did not changek stays 2. That is a result of the search and not an assumption it started from. Before 2026-08-19 this review had no executed search, so its two trials were the two somebody put on a page; they are now the two the whole 57-record programme supports.
Risk of bias downgrade follows the object s own refusalThe risk-of-bias limb on this object is REFUSED and states its consequence: 'GRADE rates down one level for risk of bias.' That instruction is followed rather than re-derived. The object's refusal is the authority on what its own absence costs.

Paper

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

Azilsartan medoxomil plus chlorthalidone against olmesartan medoxomil plus hydrochlorothiazide on change in clinic systolic blood pressure: the two trials that share both arms1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. title

Abstract

Question. In Azilsartan medoxomil plus chlorthalidone against olmesartan medoxomil plus hydrochlorothiazide on change in clinic systolic blood pressure: the two trials that share both arms, what is the effect on mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure?1

Methods. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 was searched; no search was executed against PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch); estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML (restricted maximum likelihood) estimator; and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. MmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure: mean difference -5.69 (-7.3 to -4.08) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed closely (I-squared 0%); and certainty of the evidence was low.3

Introduction

Background. This review asks: In Azilsartan medoxomil plus chlorthalidone against olmesartan medoxomil plus hydrochlorothiazide on change in clinic systolic blood pressure: the two trials that share both arms, what is the effect on mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure? It pools 2 randomised trials, against olmesartan medoxomil plus hydrochlorothiazide. The outcome pooled is mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure. Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. Registry-sourced. Every trial identity and endpoint on this object was read from its registration on the date recorded per trial.1

Sources for this section (1)

Methods — search

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: intervention="azilsartan"; study_type=interventional; no phase filter; page_size=100; count_total=true. It returned 57 record(s).1

No search was executed against PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) for this topic.2

Primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on 2026-08-18. Every point estimate and interval is the value ClinicalTrials.gov posts in the outcome's own analyses block, read on 2026-08-18, with the statistical method the registry names. Nothing is derived from arm means.3

Methods — eligibility criteria

Population: adults with essential or primary hypertension, read from the coded conditions field. Where that field names a study objective rather than a disease -- NCT01309828 declares `conditions: Safety` -- it is not assessable for this limb and the verdict falls back to the registered title, saying on its face which it rests on. Intervention: azilsartan medoxomil together with chlorthalidone in the same arm; azilsartan monotherapy is a different intervention and azilsartan with amlodipine is another. Comparator: olmesartan medoxomil together with hydrochlorothiazide. Estimand, which governs poolability and not eligibility: change from baseline in clinic systolic blood pressure, detected structurally at every rank. Criteria are derived post hoc and say so. They are narrow because the question is -- one fixed-dose combination against one other -- and narrowness is a defect only when derived backwards from the trials already present, which is why the screen ran over the whole programme rather than a shortlist.1

Each criterion above is recorded with the source it was derived from in `screening.eligibility_provenance`; none is asserted here without one.2

Methods — outcomes sought at every registered rank

Before deciding which outcomes could be combined, every trial was read at every registered rank -- primary, secondary and other -- asking: does each trial that shares both arms register a blood-pressure change outcome at any rank -- primary, secondary or other -- before concluding which trials can be combined? Asked at every registered rank and detected structurally -- a blood-pressure term plus a change term -- rather than by the two incumbents' registered phrase, which would have found the two that already agree and nothing else. Yes for the two included trials and no for the other two. Four registrations in the whole azilsartan programme carry both arms of this contrast. Two register a blood-pressure change outcome and are pooled; two register none at any rank and are eligible, not poolable. Both of those are long-term open-label safety studies -- n=837 and n=153 -- and their absence from the pool is an estimand fact, not a population one.1

Methods — synthesis

For mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML (restricted maximum likelihood) estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 , following . 0 result-level assessments were made.2

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 1 pooled outcome(s) were rated.3

Results

The pooled mean difference for mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure was -5.69 (-7.3 to -4.08) across 2 trials, against olmesartan medoxomil plus hydrochlorothiazide.1

Noted on this pool. Read this beside the estimate. This pooled outcome is identified as week 8. NCT00846365 registers its primary at week 8; NCT01033071 registers its primary at week 12 -- 'Change From Baseline in Trough, Sitting, Clinic Systolic Blood Pressure', time frame 'Baseline and Week 12'. The measurement is the same measurement in the same words; it is not taken at the same time. GRADE indirectness is rated down for it. Both trials randomise two experimental arms -- azilsartan/chlorthalidone 20-40mg and 40-80mg -- against one olmesartan/hydrochlorothiazide comparator. This object stores one effect per trial. Which dose contrast it represents, or whether the two were combined, is not established from the registrations. Recorded as unestablished rather than assumed, because a multi-arm trial contributing one row against a shared control is where control-group double counting arises. The unadjusted interval is MD -5.6912 (-7.2996 to -4.0828) mmHg and excludes no effect. This project's floored Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is -16.1181 to 4.7357 and includes it. The honest reading is narrow: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives, so this is weaker evidence against the result than the same crossing would be at larger k. Disclosed because a reader is entitled to both intervals. Stated plainly. No result-level RoB 2 assessment has been performed for either contributing result. That is recorded as unassessed, never as absent of bias, and GRADE is rated down one level for it. What would close it: RoB 2 per result on the clinic systolic pressure outcome in both registrations.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.237, on degrees of freedom 1.3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Two trials randomise the same fixed-dose combination against the same comparator and register the same continuous endpoint. Nothing had to be harmonised: this review's question was already a question, its estimand was already shared, and its arms already matched. What it lacked was any evidence that these were the only two, and the executed search of 2026-08-19 supplies it -- 57 registrations screened, 53 excluded, and only four carrying both arms of the contrast at all. The other two are long-term open-label safety studies that register no blood-pressure change outcome at any rank, so they are eligible and not poolable rather than absent. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

What this does not establish: Not that the trials are free of bias -- no RoB-2 assessment is recorded on this object. Not that the pooled value transfers outside the populations these trials enrolled. Not that the registry's posted analysis is itself correct: it is read, and reading it faithfully is a different claim from endorsing it.5

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

LOW certainty. The two trials agree closely and both are quadruple-masked, so the downgrades are not for inconsistency or for anything shown about how the trials were run. They are for a risk-of-bias assessment this review has not performed, and for the two trials measuring the same quantity at different times -- week 8 on one registration and week 12 on the other, under an outcome this object identifies as week 8.2

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step3
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
mmHg change from baseline in trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressureLOW2risk of bias -- the risk-of-bias limb is REFUSED on this object, and its refusal names its own consequence: 'GRADE rates down one level for risk of bias.' No result-level RoB 2 assessment has been performed for either contributing result, and the refusal records that as unassessed, never as absent of bias. The downgrade is for what we have not done, not for anything shown about these trials -- both register quadruple masking including the outcomes assessor, which is the strongest masking either could record. (move: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s)); inconsistency -- tau-squared is exactly zero, Q 0.2375 on 1 df, p = 0.6260, I-squared 0.00%. The two effects -- -6.1 (-8.4 to -3.8) and -5.3 (-7.6 to -3.1) mmHg -- agree in size and in direction. Downgrading here would manufacture a caution the numbers do not support. (move: no downgrade); indirectness -- the pooled outcome is called week 8 and one of its two trials registers its primary at week 12. NCT00846365's registered time frame is 'Baseline and Week 8'; NCT01033071's is 'Baseline and Week 12'. The measurement is identical in words -- trough, sitting, clinic systolic blood pressure -- but an antihypertensive effect at eight weeks and at twelve weeks are not the same quantity, and the outcome's own identifier asserts week 8 for both. Recorded and not separately rated: both trials randomise two experimental dose arms against one comparator and this object stores one effect per trial; which dose contrast that is, or whether the two were combined, is not established from the registrations. (move: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s)); imprecision -- k = 2. This project's floored Hartung-Knapp interval is -16.1181 to 4.7357 on t = 12.7062 with 1 degree of freedom and it includes no effect, where the unadjusted interval -7.2996 to -4.0828 excludes it. A downgrade is warranted on that alone. It is not applied, and the reason is stated rather than hidden: at k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives the adjustment, so the crossing is weak evidence of imprecision in either direction. Note also what is not used: metafor's RAW unfloored interval here is -10.7725 to -0.6100 and does exclude no effect. That is not this project's interval and it is not cited as one. (move: LOW to very LOW -- warranted and not applied, see reason); publication bias -- k = 2. A funnel plot and its asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is not assessable rather than 'undetected'. (move: Not assessable -- no rating applied)

Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1

The withholding question, asked at every rank

does each trial that shares BOTH arms register a blood-pressure CHANGE outcome at ANY rank -- primary, secondary or other -- before concluding which trials can be combined?

YES FOR THE TWO INCLUDED TRIALS AND NO FOR THE OTHER TWO. Four registrations in the whole azilsartan programme carry both arms of this contrast. Two register a blood-pressure change outcome and are pooled; two register none at any rank and are ELIGIBLE, NOT POOLABLE. Both of those are long-term open-label SAFETY studies -- n=837 and n=153 -- and their absence from the pool is an estimand fact, not a population one.

Asked at EVERY registered rank and detected STRUCTURALLY -- a blood-pressure term plus a change term -- rather than by the two incumbents' registered phrase, which would have found the two that already agree and nothing else.

Heterogeneity: Undefined: no between-study variance was estimated because no model was run.

Published-meta comparison — PENDING_EXTERNAL_RESOLUTION

Denominator: —. Not yet established. Establishing it requires resolving published syntheses' included-sets to REGISTRATION IDs. A second lane has validated that pipeline (stated-k table identification plus two-hop citation->PMID->registration) and is running it now.

Explicitly not done: CITATION-STRING MATCHING. It would produce a comparison-shaped answer tonight and it is not identity: two syntheses citing the same trial under different labels would read as different, and the same label on different trials as the same. That is the substitution class this project audits for.
